sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 40 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. This standing-start run begins at the first paired edge station and ends at the last; original timing metadata are retained. Finish speed is unconstrained, with no stopping zone modelled. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Road-limit estimates from the pinned Environment Agency one-metre last-return laser-intensity raster captured 30 December 2019, checked against the historic 2015 point-cloud visualization and satellite context. Intensity is reflected laser energy, not an aerial photograph. Approximate 36 m observation spacing, raster resolution and sparse interpolation limit accuracy. Inner means driver-left and outer driver-right along this open run. The starting edge follows the adjoining visible road lines across the paved entrance; right-side limits at the building entrances near stations 324 and 336 interpolate between visible neighbouring edges rather than asserting roof or apron observations. The final widened paved bay is retained. Distinct endpoints follow the saved trace and are not surveyed timing or stopping points. Terrain remains the existing estimated profile, banking unknown, rendered curbs illustrative.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed directly from complete, sparse image measurements on the existing trace cross-sections. All intervals interpolate between image anchors; they are not automatic detections or a continuous edge survey. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. Isolated missing pixels inside the road are not filled or used as boundary evidence. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. These borders have not been formally verified.
